I'm racing in my first triathlon in September. I'm in OK shape physically and mentally.

Besides not having any open water swim training (which I'm trying to schedule), I'm comfortable with each event- but I want to be MORE than comfortable and confident. Any tips on this next training push? Should I be going for distance? Or speed and strength?

It sounds like you are comfortable with the events and the distances. Then the next things I would work on are the following.

  1. Do some practice "bricks". This means a swim followed directly by a bike or a bike followed directly by a run. You will find that it feels weird immediately after the switch. With a little practice it becomes normal. I bike commute most days of the week and then I will go for an evening run. I don't even think about it any more.

  2. Practice transitions. This is different from bricks. Here you are thinking about exactly how you layout all your gear. elite athletes will practice transitions so that they can get faster. You should practice transitions so that you are less prone to forgetting something. Don't want to be 2 miles into the bike and realize you forgot you sunglasses.

  3. Have fun. Should be a blast.

edit: formatting

Bricks are your friends. Swim then bike; bike then run. I find the hardest is to bike then run because my legs feel really weird and off. Oh, and practice your transitions!

There's lots of debate on time vs. distance. I'm training for time right now, but I've only switched to that in the last two weeks (I'm a week out from my race). I trained for distance first because I'm a nervous Nelly and don't ever think I can do the distances. By doing the distances (with unlimited time), I have the knowledge in the back of my brain that I can physically do it. The past two weeks I've trained by time (hour swim, hour bike--hour bike, 40min run) and let the distances take care of themselves--which surprisingly, they have.

I guess my point is, it depends on you and your comfort level and what you want. I have no illusions of making the podium, so strength is my goal. You, on-the-other-hand, may be podium bound (which is really cool). Speed should be your thing.

I wish you all the luck in the world for your upcoming race. And congrats on being there physically and mentally (like I said, I'm a week out and still don't quite have the mental thing). Rock on!!
